name: Rain
label: Dischord
lede: Rain lasted about a year, cut six songs with [[Ian MacKaye]] and broke up before any of them came out. [[Guy Picciotto]] put the record out three years later, on a label he ran himself.

eras.title: Older bassist, first-timers
eras.text: Revolution Summer had turned DC hardcore melodic and inward in 1985, and a younger crowd took the hint. Rain was a trio: Bert Queiroz, who'd already done the rounds of the scene, and Jon Kirschten and Eli Janney, in their first real band.

years.src: Dischord · Some Will Never Know · Wikipedia · Exclaim!
years.h: Rain starts as a trio in 1986, guitar and vocals up front
years.p: Jon Kirschten sings and plays guitar, [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]] plays bass and [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] plays drums. Dischord calls them one of the key bands of Revolution Summer's second wave.
years.xp:
Queiroz had the pedigree: the Untouchables, [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]], Double O and Second Wind. For Janney and Kirschten, Rain was the first proper band, though Wikipedia and Some Will Never Know both have Kirschten passing briefly through [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]].

The sound followed the path [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] had cut: melodic, introspective, still loud. Reviewers later reached for [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]] and early R.E.M.

eras.title: Two sessions, one year
eras.text: Everything Rain recorded, it recorded in 1987, in two studios. By the time the second set of tapes was done, the band was too.

years.h: Four songs on tape at WGNS, January 1987
years.p: The three-piece cuts a demo at WGNS, the studio run by [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]]'s [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]]. One of the four, In Rain, never makes it onto the later record.
years.xp:
Dischord puts the session in January. Some Will Never Know counts four songs on the tape, all from the trio lineup, before Scott McCloud arrived.

The same site says the 1990 12" carries one demo track alongside the Inner Ear material, which would account for six songs from a session it counts at five.

years.h: Scott McCloud comes over from Soulside on second guitar
years.p: [[Scott McCloud|11e1e118-8744-45f0-9c37-dc4944541134]], already in [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], joins as second guitarist and singer ahead of the Inner Ear session with Ian MacKaye.

years.h: Rain are done before the Inner Ear tapes come out
years.p: Dischord dates the end to 1987, not long after the session with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]. Nothing is released yet, and nothing will be for another two years.

eras.title: Released by a friend
eras.text: The songs surfaced anyway: one on a Dischord compilation, then all six on a 12" from Guy Picciotto's Peterbilt label. McCloud and Janney were already onto Girls Against Boys.

years.h: McCloud and Janney start Girls Against Boys
years.p: Half of Rain's final lineup, singer-guitarist Scott McCloud and drummer Eli Janney, form a new band. It outlasts Rain by decades and ends up on a major label in the '90s.

yt: Worlds At War, from the 1987 Inner Ear session
years.h: The first place most people hear Rain: a DC comp
years.p: Dischord puts Rain's Worlds At War on its 1989 compilation State of the Union, one song from a band that no longer exists.

years.src: Dischord · Some Will Never Know · Rain on Bandcamp · Wikipedia
yt: Snakeout, from La Vache Qui Rit
years.h: The 1987 session finally comes out, as La Vache Qui Rit
years.p: Rain cut six songs at Inner Ear Studios with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] in 1987. [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]]'s Peterbilt label issues them as a 12" in 1990, three years after the band split.
years.xp:
The title is French for the laughing-cow cheese. The six songs: That Time Of Year, End Of My Mind, Snakeout, Worlds At War, Around The Axis and Rivers. It stayed out of print for most of the next two decades.

The count is a little muddy. Dischord says the MacKaye session was at Inner Ear; Some Will Never Know counts five songs from it and says the 12" adds one demo track. Rain's Bandcamp dates all six to 1987.

eras.title: The cow laughs again
eras.text: Dischord and Peterbilt put the record back out on CD, and a band most people knew as the thing before Girls Against Boys got reviewed like a new release.

years.cap: La Vache Qui Rit, Dischord/Peterbilt CD reissue
years.h: La Vache Qui Rit comes back on CD in 2007
years.p: Dischord and Peterbilt reissue Rain's only record, remastered, after years out of print. Exclaim!'s Vish Khanna hears Rites of Spring, Mission of Burma and early R.E.M. in it.
years.xp:
Khanna also picks up a poppy streak running under the frantic parts, which he says is paired with a faith in organic textures. His review ran September 24, 2007.

The record now sits on Dischord's Bandcamp with the rest of the catalog.

years.cap: Girls Against Boys, Touch and Go 25th anniversary block party, Chicago, September 2006
years.p: Janney and McCloud: [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]]. Queiroz: Manifesto, then [[Thunderball|8579d918-835b-4c1d-ac00-45a7f4a8763a]]. Kirschten: The Chris Bald 96, Special K and Las Mordidas.
